commandEditor.name: Name
commandEditor.renameHint: The trigger viewers type in chat. Renaming keeps the response and settings.
commandEditor.responsePlaceholder: What the bot replies… insert variables below.
commandEditor.linesHint: Up to {max} lines; each line is sent as its own chat message.
commandEditor.tokTarget: first argument, e.g. a mentioned user
commandEditor.tokChannel: the channel the command runs in
commandEditor.tokWord: word 1 typed after the command; {2} is the next one, up to {30}
commandEditor.tokWordsFrom: word 2 through to the end, as one string
commandEditor.tokUserId: the Twitch user ID of whoever ran the command
commandEditor.tokUserLogin: their lowercase login, not their display name
commandEditor.tokCommand: the command’s own name, without the “!”
commandEditor.tokCounter: bumps the named counter and shows its new value
commandEditor.tokRandom: a random number from 1 to 100, or {random:min-max}
commandEditor.tokChoice: picks one of the comma-separated options at random
commandEditor.tokMath: evaluates a small sum: + - * / and parentheses
commandEditor.tokQueryString: everything typed after the command, URL-encoded for a data source
commandEditor.tokQueryEscape: URL-encodes the text you put after the colon
commandEditor.tokPathEscape: URL-encodes the text for a path, not a query
commandEditor.tokRepeat: repeats a phrase n times (up to 20, one chat line)
commandEditor.tokCountdown: how long until that date (YYYY-MM-DD, or a full timestamp)
commandEditor.tokIf: one text or another: {if:name:when it has something:when it does not}, or {if:name=value:…:…} for an exact match. Variables do not work inside the two texts
commandEditor.tokFollowage: how long they have followed the channel (Followage module)
commandEditor.tokAccountAge: how old their Twitch account is (Account age module)
commandEditor.tokPoints: their points balance, or {points:login} for someone else (Loyalty)
commandEditor.tokPointsName: your channel’s name for its points (Loyalty)
commandEditor.tokWatchTime: how long they have watched, in the same words as !uptime (Loyalty)
commandEditor.tokCount: reads a counter without adding to it, unlike {counter:…} (Loyalty)
commandEditor.tokUses: how many times this command has been used, not counting this one (approximate)
commandEditor.tokQuote: a random saved quote, or {quote:12} for a numbered one (Quotes module)
commandEditor.tokTime: your local time, on the clock face you set (Local time module)
commandEditor.tokSong: the track playing right now, or {song.title} / {song.artist} (Song requests)
commandEditor.tokChatters: how many people have talked in chat recently
commandEditor.tokRandomChatter: one of them, picked at random (never you, never the bot)
commandEditor.tokEmoteList: every global 7TV emote code, space-separated; {bttvemotes} and {ffzemotes} too (cut to fit one line)
commandEditor.tokRandomEmote: one emote code picked at random from those global sets
commandEditor.tokUptime: how long you have been live, empty when you are offline (!uptime toggle)
commandEditor.tokTitle: your current stream title, or {title:someone} for another channel (!title toggle)
commandEditor.tokGame: the category you are streaming, or {game:someone} for another channel (!game toggle)
commandEditor.tokChannelViewers: how many people are watching right now, 0 when you are offline
commandEditor.fallbackHint: Add | and some text inside any variable for a default when it comes back empty: {touser|everyone}.
commandEditor.restrictPlaceholder: Twitch user ID. Only they can run it

import.fossabotDesc: Type your channel name and your public Fossabot commands page is read for you. No sign-in, no token.
instrFossabot: Open your Fossabot commands page: fossabot.com/yourchannel/commands. It is public, so there is nothing to sign in to.
Your channel name is the part of that address before /commands, normally your Twitch login.
Type that channel name below to continue.
Only what that page lists comes over. Commands hidden from the directory, timers, keywords and cooldowns are not published there, so they stay behind.
import.instrHint: Follow these steps in {source}, then provide what is asked below. Your file is read right here in the browser. Nothing is uploaded until you preview.
instrMoobot: Sign in at moobot.ai and open your dashboard.
Click “Export this dashboard to a file” and save the .json file.
Choose that file below to continue.
instrNightbot: Click “Connect Nightbot” below. You'll be sent to nightbot.tv to sign in and approve access.
Approve the request (commands, timers and spam protection, read for this import only) and you'll land right back here.
Hit Continue and pick what to import.
instrSe: Sign in at streamelements.com and open your dashboard.
Go to Account Settings → Channels, or use the direct link below.
In your browser's developer tools → Network tab, click any request to api.streamelements.com and copy the token after “Bearer ” in its Authorization header.
Paste the JWT below to continue.
instrSl: On the computer where the StreamLabs Chatbot desktop app runs, close the app first so the database is fully written.
Locate Chatbot.db and upload it below to continue.
instrWizebot: In your Wizebot panel, open the Streaming Website section and turn it on if it is off. Your command list is only published while that site is enabled.
Your channel login is the subdomain of that site: in yourchannel.streaming.lv, it is yourchannel.
Type that login below to continue.

Only commands that post chat text come over. Screen animations and sound-only commands are skipped, and when a command carries a public description, Wizebot publishes that instead of its chat message, so check the review step.

onboarding.title: Welcome aboard 🥯
onboarding.intro: You're connected and the bot can see your chat. Here is the short path to fully live, one page at a time:
onboarding.consentBody: Please accept the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy before proceeding.
onboarding.consentLabel: I agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy
onboarding.langBody: Pick the language for your console with the switch below. You can change it any time on the Settings page.
onboarding.step1Body: Type this in your Twitch chat. Without mod status, Twitch silences the bot in follower-only, sub-only, and slow-mode chats. It would look like it just stopped working.
onboarding.step2Body: The Commands page is where every !command lives. Build one there and the live chat rehearsal shows exactly what the bot will say before you save.
onboarding.step3Body: The Modules page holds optional extras like Auto Shoutout for incoming raids. One toggle each, configured in a minute.
onboarding.importBody: Coming from StreamElements, Moobot or StreamLabs Chatbot? The Import page brings your commands, timers and the rest over automatically instead of rebuilding them by hand.
